notes: Stability-budget input -- THE CRUX TERM: a WSL-class 1 mOhm shunt carries a ~0.5 mOhm/1000 h load-life ADDITIVE, the SAME ORDER as the 1 mOhm dV/dI signal to be resolved over weeks (NB: 0.5 mOhm is the FULL 1000-h test-endpoint figure; a 2-week trend window sees some fraction of it, and aging is NOT necessarily linear -- the in-situ multi-week benchmark OQ measures the real rate, which is exactly why it gates the Standard verdict), plus copper-terminal-dominated TCR (+/-275 ppm/C at the 1 mOhm class; TIER-BOUNDARY: CONFIRMED AT THE DATASHEET 2026-06-10 per the owner's 'confirm is the right verb' -- the Vishay 30100 TCR table binds tiers by NOMINAL resistance-value ranges ('+/-75 for 7 mOhm to 500 mOhm ... +/-400 for 0.5 mOhm to 0.99 mOhm', vendored lib/datasheets/WSL-30100.pdf) and tolerance is an orthogonal ordering code (D/F/J), so a NOMINAL 1 mOhm part stays in the 275 tier regardless of tolerance -- the boundary concern is moot; the full table also carries intermediate +/-110 and +/-150 tiers the dive's three-tier summary skipped; TRANSPARENCY: the 275 tier's 2.9 mOhm UPPER bound is inferred from adjacency to the ~3 mOhm lower bound of the 150 tier, not directly quoted from the primary table row) -- this is why the shunt BOM choice decides the Standard dV/dI verdict (dvdi.requirement_tier_verdict).
